The short grievance of the Petitioner is as to the name of Government of India being entered in the property records in respect of his lands and also the alleged frugality of the compensation paid for using the subsoil for laying a pipeline.
2. After service of notice, the 1st Respondent is represented by the Panel Counsel; 2nd Respondent Special Deputy Commissioner, Competent Authority is represented by the Senior Panel Counsel.

Both they oppose the Writ Petition contending that land of the Petitioner is not taken out at all;
subsoil has been used for laying the pipeline under the provisions of Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962.

entities.text: Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The 1st Respondent has filed the Statement of Objections contending that 10% of guideline value of the subject property has been paid to the Petitioner by way of compensation for using the subsoil of his land u/s 10(4) of this Act.

If Petitioner has grievance as to the inadequacy of the compensation, it is open to him to approach the District Judge under Rule 10(5) of Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Rules, 1963.

entities.text: Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Rules, 1963
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: So contending, they seek dismissal of the Writ Petition.

3. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition Papers, this Court is inclined to grant indulgence in the matter inasmuch as the ownership of the subject land would still continue with the Petitioner himself as has been submitted by the learned Advocates appearing for the Respondents rightly.
If that be so, the 2nd Respondent-Special Deputy Commissioner ought to have ensured that name of Central Government does not figure in the property records in respect of the subject land.

sentences.text:
The second grievance, i.e., inadequacy of compensation, Petitioner has got an alternate &
efficacious remedy as provided under Rule 10(5) of the 1963 Rules and in this connection, he can make a petition to the jurisdictional District Judge within a period prescribed by law.

Learned counsel for the 2nd Respondent points out that the period prescribed for filing petition is 90 days from the date the compensation has been paid to him and years having now rolled, nothing can be made out.
This court shares the same view.
It is stated by the sages of law that law and this court does not come to the aid of sleepy & tardy since delay defeats equity.

In the above circumstances, this Writ Petition is partly allowed; 2nd Respondent is directed to ensure that name of the Petitioner alone would continue in the property records after deleting that of the Central Government.
This has to be accomplished immediately and compliance report should be filed to the Registrar General of this Court within an outer limit of 60 days failing which the incumbent of office of the Spl.
Deputy Commissioner shall be personally liable to pay Rs.2,000/- per day to the Petitioner for the first 30 days and Rs.3,000/- thereafter.
